questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'break' statement inside a loop in Python?
options: To skip the rest of the current iteration

questions.question: Which loop construction has the potential to lead to an infinite loop if not properly controlled?

Consider the following code snippet:

count = 0
while count < 3:
    print(count)
    count -= 1

What will happen when this code is executed?
options: It creates an infinite loop printing decreasing numbers
It results in a runtime error because subtraction in a while loop is not allowed
It prints nothing because the loop condition is never met
questions.correct_answer: It creates an infinite loop printing decreasing numbers

questions.question: Which type of loop is generally preferred when the number of iterations is known before the loop starts?
What is the purpose of the 'else' clause in a loop construct in Python?
options: It always executes after the loop body regardless of conditions
It executes only if the loop completes normally without encountering a break
It executes whenever the loop encounters a continue statement
There is no else clause applicable to loops in Python
questions.correct_answer: It executes only if the loop completes normally without encountering a break
